attributes.location: along DRXed grain boundaries, especially at triple junctions

evidence.quote: The selected area diffraction pattern in Fig. 3a confirms that these particles are of the expected Mg17Al12 phase.

attributes.location: inside equiaxed grains and grain boundaries

evidence.quote: The relative amount (in atomic percent) of major elements in the precipitate is 9.32% Mg, 56.90% Al, and 33.78% Mn.

attributes.morphology: equiaxed fine DRXed grains and elongated coarse unDRXed grains

evidence.quote: the as-extruded alloy exhibits a bimodal microstructure consisting of equiaxed fine DRXed grains (the dark area in Fig. 2a) and elongated coarse unDRXed grains (the white area in Fig. 2a).
this region has an ultra-fine structure, with a grain size of ~0.4 µm

attributes.morphology: fibers with {0001} plane and <10-10> direction parallel to ED

evidence.quote: Both alloys exhibit a basal fiber texture that is typical of extruded Mg alloys, in which the {0001} plane and <10-10> direction are preferentially oriented parallel to the ED. However, it is clearly seen that the maximum intensity (Imax) of the LTSS-extruded alloy (5.1) is much higher than that of the alloy extruded at a higher temperature and speed (1.7).

attributes.morphology: fibers with {0001} plane and <10-10> direction parallel to ED

evidence.quote: Both alloys exhibit a basal fiber texture that is typical of extruded Mg alloys, in which the {0001} plane and <10-10> direction are preferentially oriented parallel to the ED. However, it is clearly seen that the maximum intensity (Imax) of the LTSS-extruded alloy (5.1) is much higher than that of the alloy extruded at a higher temperature and speed (1.7).
the cast alloy consists predominantly of α-Mg grains, with a macro-segregation of the solute element and intermetallic compounds occurring mostly at the grain boundaries.

the large number of nano-sized Mg17Al12 particles that are dynamically precipitated during LTSS extrusion are considered likely to play a significant role in restricting the growth of the DRXed grains by pinning the grain boundaries, thereby leading to a remarkably refined grain structure.
the grain size of the homogenized alloy is significantly refined by extrusion, indicating that DRX does indeed occur during this process.
dislocation pile-ups around these fine precipitates can act as nuclei for DRX
the activation of twinning at low extrusion temperatures can promotes the nucleation of DRXed grains at the twin interfaces
yield asymmetry results from a difference in the predominant deformation mechanism; i.e., basal slip during tension and {10-12} twinning under compression.
